purpose: Structured FTC Walmart wire-transfer refund ledger distinguishing reported check dispatch from consumer cashing, adequacy, and later financial recovery.

events.geography: United States; consumers affected by fraud-induced Walmart wire transfers
events.date_precision: Day precision for FTC payment announcement; recipients are instructed to cash checks within 90 days
events.denominator: 65,022 affected consumers receiving checks; aggregate recipient count, not a retained person-level denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the official FTC press release, Walmart case page, and timeline record
events.missingness: No recipient identifiers, individual check amount, mailing or delivery result, cashing, returned check, reissue, original transfer loss, fraud recovery, household effect, trust, switching, or exit are retained
events.exposure: The FTC alleged Walmart failed to implement effective anti-fraud policies, train employees adequately, and warn customers about fraud connected to its wire-transfer services
events.alternatives_before_action: Consumers could stop or question a transfer, seek provider or law-enforcement help, use another transfer route, or pursue private recovery; person-level feasible alternatives and effort are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Fraud-induced transfers could impose direct monetary loss, urgency, fear, and recovery effort; the public record does not quantify individual loss or household consequences
events.choice_or_response: The FTC announced that checks were being sent and instructed recipients to cash them within 90 days; individual delivery, cashing, reissue, or continued use of Walmart transfer services is not observed
events.person_or_actor_with_control: FTC and refund administrator control distribution; Walmart controlled the original service and prospective anti-fraud practices; recipients control cashing within the stated window under unknown access constraints
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The FTC announced more than $9.8 million in payments to 65,022 consumers following Walmart's 2025 $10 million settlement and required prospective anti-fraud actions
events.remedy_receipt: Checks are reported as sent, but individual delivery, cashing, and receipt are not verified
events.durability_followup: No recipient-level fraud recurrence, account correction, residual loss, trust, switching, or exit record is public in the payment announcement
events.immediate_outcome: A reported consumer-refund distribution is underway with a defined 90-day cashing window
events.protected_outcome: The distribution may return some loss to affected consumers, but individual receipt and adequacy are not established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Original fraud loss, recovery effort, time, fear, and residual household burden remain unmeasured
events.cost_risk_transfer: The remedy shifts some financial responsibility toward Walmart and the administrator, while delivery, cashing, and residual-loss risk remain with consumers until receipt is established
events.later_outcome: Reported check dispatch is observed, but cashing, reissue, adequacy, fraud recurrence, household recovery, trust, switching, and exit remain unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: The agency attributes alleged control failures to Walmart, but consumer-level fairness, blame, trust, or legitimacy change is not measured
events.public_or_collective_response: FTC enforcement and refund administration are observed; consumer organizing, complaint persistence, and political action are not linked
events.counterexample: Checks sent to an affected-consumer group can coexist with failed delivery, uncashed or returned checks, inadequate amounts, or continued fraud exposure
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official FTC press release dated 2026-10-15 (https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2026/10/ftc-sends-more-98-million-consumers-harmed-walmarts-failure-stop-scammers-used-its-wire-transfer), Walmart case page (https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/cases-proceedings/182-3012-walmart-ftc-v), and official timeline record (https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/cases-proceedings/walmart-ftc-v-timeline-item-2026-10-15). The public records establish reported dispatch, aggregate amount, recipient count, and cashing window, not individual delivery, cashing, adequacy, or later outcome

arrows.evidence: The FTC case record describes alleged control failures, the 2025 settlement, monetary judgment, and prospective anti-fraud obligations
arrows.counterexample: The enforcement record does not identify every affected transfer or consumer-level loss
arrows.remaining_gap: Consumer-level transaction, loss, notice, and recovery-effort linkage

arrows.evidence: The FTC says it is sending more than $9.8 million in checks to 65,022 affected consumers
arrows.counterexample: Reported dispatch does not establish mailing success, receipt, or a stable person-level denominator
arrows.remaining_gap: Recipient identity, delivery, failed mail, address update, reissue, and individual amount

arrows.evidence: Recipients are instructed to cash checks within 90 days, but the public announcement reports no later cashing result
arrows.counterexample: A sent check can be uncashed, returned, inaccessible, or delayed
arrows.remaining_gap: Cashing, receipt date, returned check, reissue, account access, and amount

arrows.to: financial recovery, fraud recurrence, trust, switching, or exit
arrows.evidence: The FTC payment and case records provide no recipient-level later household or behavioral follow-up
arrows.counterexample: A cashed refund does not establish adequate recovery, restored security, or changed use of transfer services
arrows.remaining_gap: Original loss, adequacy, household recovery, recurrence, trust, switching, and exit

boundary: This ledger establishes an official aggregate refund distribution with reported check dispatch and a 90-day cashing window. It does not establish recipient-level delivery, cashing, adequate recovery, fraud prevention, trust, switching, or exit.
storage_boundary: Only compact official page-derived fields and source URLs are retained; no recipient identifiers, mailing records, payment file, or raw personal data is downloaded.
